page: Amazon Web Services r8gb.12xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by custom AWS Graviton processors. Built on the arm64 architecture, this instance features 48 dedicated physical cores utilizing the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 model running at 2.8 GHz. It is configured with 384.0 GB of system memory, yielding a ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per core. The CPU cache configuration includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache. This instance operates on the Nitro hypervisor and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps, though it contains no local NVMe storage.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and memory subsystem performance. In stress-ng multi-core tests, the instance achieved a strong score of 81876.27, while its Geekbench multi-core score reached a top-tier 23666.0. Memory bandwidth is a primary strength, with read-only large block transfers reaching a top-tier 434.99 GB/sec and write large block transfers at 216.28 GB/sec. Passmark database operations scored in the top tier at 47920.83, and Redis SET operations reached 101.9 million operations per second. Single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the average to strong ranges.

The lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which may introduce latency tradeoffs for disk-heavy operations. However, the high memory-to-core ratio and top-tier memory bandwidth make this instance highly cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads that do not require local disk caching. The dedicated physical cores without hyperthreading ensure predictable compute performance. This hardware profile is suited for large-scale in-memory databases, caching layers, multi-threaded data decompression, and memory-intensive enterprise applications.
